description: The pause/resume WRITE rule, as a cross-repo fixture. The registry's metadata.paused is the single source of truth and BOTH doors (wanxing facade console, 壹座 packs surface) write it — so the payload they write must be identical, not merely equivalent. The one place it is easy to get subtly wrong: resuming REMOVES the key rather than writing false, because every reader tests `=== true` and a lingering explicit false is a different shape that the next consumer will trip over.
target: PUT /api/agents{agentPath} with this body (falling back to POST /api/agents/register on refusal)

cases.name: pause an entry that has no metadata yet
cases.note: metadata is created; only the paused key is added.

cases.name: pause an entry that already carries other metadata
cases.note: Sibling metadata MUST survive: a pause that drops the rhythm would silently unschedule the agent.

cases.name: resume a paused entry — the key is REMOVED, not set to false
cases.note: THE case this fixture exists for. `metadata.paused === undefined` is the resumed state; writing `paused: false` leaves a shape no reader expects.

cases.name: resume an entry that was never paused (idempotent)
cases.note: Resuming a running agent is a no-op, not an error.

cases.name: resume an entry whose metadata becomes empty
cases.note: Recorded as the CURRENT behaviour: the metadata object stays present but empty (this implementation never drops it). Pinned so a future refactor is a deliberate change, not an accident.
